details:
Q1: Open PR #9246 already targets this same "closed-reader test" failure on ubuntu-26.04. How should this triage issue relate to it?
Choices:
A) Treat this issue as a duplicate of #9246: don't change any code here, and once #9246 merges, update PR #8960's branch from the default branch and re-run CI. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Fix it independently in this issue's own PR, even though it may conflict with or duplicate #9246.
C) Re-run CI on PR #8960 only, treating it as a runner flake, and change no code.
**Note:** C does not fix the cause. uutils `cat` returns 0 every time on ubuntu-26.04, so the test will fail on every run there, not now and then.
Q2: If code changes here (Q1:B, or if #9246 is closed without merging), where should the fix go?
Choices:
A) Fix `gh_retry` in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`, including the copies the contract tests check (the inline review_autofix copies and `gh_retry_to_file` if it resends output the same way). When it resends the saved output, a closed reader should give a non-zero status no matter which `cat` the runner has. Keep the test's assertion as it is. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Change only the test so it accepts `rc=0` when the runner's `cat` is uutils coreutils.
C) Pin the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to an older runner image (for example `ubuntu-24.04`) instead of `ubuntu-latest`.
**Note:** B weakens the test, which the issue explicitly forbids ("Do not loosen the test"). It would also leave production `gh_retry` callers reporting success when their output was never delivered.
